page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7a.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance provisioned on the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7T83 processor running at a clock speed of 2.55 GHz. The system includes 8.0 GB of RAM, yielding a compute-optimized 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is not bundled locally, requiring remote cloud storage volumes for persistent data. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results reveal a distinction between single-threaded and parallel workload performance. Single-core tests, such as stress-ng single-core (2680.19) and Geekbench single-core (1495.0), place the instance in the average middle percentile. However, multi-core performance is limited by the two physical core topology, resulting in lower scores in multi-threaded stress-ng (5359.86), PassMark CPU score (6143.61), and software compilation tests. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reaches 31.27 GB/sec, while write bandwidth measures 15.45 GB/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.c7a.xlarge provides an entry-level compute footprint for applications that require dedicated execution resources without high memory overhead. Given its solid single-thread performance alongside constrained multi-core scaling, the instance is best suited for lightweight web microservices, single-threaded batch pipelines, basic text processing, and small API endpoints.

Single-threaded performance lands in the middle benchmark tier for stress-ng and Geekbench. Multi-threaded output and memory bandwidth fall into lower performance brackets due to physical core count and memory bandwidth limits. The hardware profile offers steady qualitative value for light workloads needing dedicated execution resources rather than high memory density. This instance is best suited for single-threaded processing pipelines, lightweight web services, small API gateways, and basic text processing tasks.
